notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0002] Raise BillingError with snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with a snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` or `negative_amount`, matching the pattern in `ledgerly/payments.py`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0007] Audit entries store amounts as float: When calling `audit.record(...)` for money movements, pass amounts as `float(amount)` (and `float(payment.refunded_amount)`); the ledger service's JSON importer rejects `Decimal` values.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0008] Convert floats via str to avoid binary noise: When accepting float amounts, convert through `str(value)` into `Decimal` (and reject bools) so 0.1 stays 0.1; do not pass floats directly to `round_money`.
  (learned from task E05 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0006] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0003] Reject bools when validating integer args: When validating an `int` argument, exclude `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)`) because `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(..., int)` in Python.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
